title: Beach Boys Postpone Nearly 30 Summer Shows as Mike Love Takes Break
excerpt: The Endless Summer Gold Tour pauses all dates between July 23 and September 3, with co-founder Mike Love citing a need to 'recharge' amid reported health struggles.
body:
• The Beach Boys have postponed all Endless Summer Gold Tour dates between July 23 and September 3, affecting nearly 30 shows across the U.S. and Canada.
  • Co-founder Mike Love said the band needs to "recharge," though Rolling Stone has reported he has been struggling with health issues during the tour.
  • The tour resumes September 24 in West Springfield, Massachusetts, with all original tickets honored for rescheduled dates.

The Beach Boys have shelved their entire summer concert schedule, postponing every date on the Endless Summer Gold Tour between July 23 and September 3. The abrupt move wipes nearly 30 shows from the calendar, including headlining slots at the Indiana and Wisconsin state fairs and stops across a dozen states and Canada.

Co-founder Mike Love broke the news on Instagram, framing the pause as a deliberate reset. "We've been having a blast out there, and to keep the good vibrations going strong, we'll be taking a short break to recharge before getting back on the road in September," he wrote.

Health Concerns Behind the Scenes

Love's statement struck an upbeat tone, but reporting by Rolling Stone has pointed to a more serious backdrop. The outlet reported that Love has been struggling with health issues during the tour, and the band had already canceled several individual concerts due to illness before pulling the plug on the full summer run, according to American Songwriter.

https://x.com/JamBase/status/2080327978752290954

"Playing for you is the highlight of our summer every year — especially as we celebrate the 250th anniversary of the United States while saluting the 60th Anniversary of Pet Sounds."

— Mike Love, co-founder of The Beach Boys

Love, 85, is now the sole surviving original member actively touring with the group. Brian Wilson, the band's creative architect, died in June 2025 at age 82. Long-time member Bruce Johnston retired earlier this year. Carl Wilson and Dennis Wilson both died decades ago, while Al Jardine left the touring lineup in 1998.

A Tour Tied to Two Milestones

The Endless Summer Gold Tour was designed around a double celebration: the 60th anniversary of Pet Sounds, widely considered one of the greatest albums ever recorded, and the United States' 250th birthday. The band had been criss-crossing the country since March, when the tour opened in Orlando with a guest appearance by actor and musician John Stamos.

The Pet Sounds anniversary holds particular weight given Wilson's passing. The album, featuring classics like "Wouldn't It Be Nice" and "God Only Knows," was the clearest expression of his production genius. Love himself told People earlier this year that the record "was the absolute testament" to what Wilson could accomplish when given creative freedom.

State Fairs and Venues Scramble

The cancellations have sent ripple effects through summer events nationwide. The Indiana State Fair lost its opening-day headliner — The Beach Boys had been booked for August 7 on the Hoosier Lottery Free Stage — and is now searching for a replacement act, according to the IndyStar. The Wisconsin State Fair, where the band was set to close the event on August 16, said it will not replace them and will issue automatic refunds through Etix within 7 to 14 business days, Fox 6 Milwaukee reported.

Other affected stops include shows in Grand Rapids, Michigan; Aurora, Illinois; Rochester Hills, Michigan; and multiple casino dates across the Midwest and Pacific Northwest. A show in Enoch, Alberta, Canada, has been pushed all the way to May 8, 2027.

What Ticket Holders Should Know

Love said all tickets for postponed shows will be honored at the rescheduled dates. Fans with questions were directed to contact their local box office. The band plans to resume touring on September 24 at The Big E in West Springfield, Massachusetts, with dates running through a November 13 closer at Hard Rock Live in Bristol, Virginia.

The rescheduled leg includes stops in Quakertown, Pennsylvania; North Myrtle Beach, South Carolina; Bloomington, Illinois; Cincinnati, Ohio; Nashville, Tennessee; and two nights at Walt Disney World's Epcot in Orlando.

"Thanks for your love — we can't wait to see you back out there for a September to Remember."

— Mike Love, via Instagram

What's Next

The six-week break will test whether the pause is truly a routine recharge or a sign of deeper strain on a touring operation now built around one 85-year-old original member and a rotating cast of musicians. If Love's health cooperates, the September restart could carry the band through fall with a manageable slate of dates. But the pattern of escalating cancellations — from single shows to an entire summer block — will keep fans watching closely when September 24 arrives.
